expectations.text: Produces complete, self-contained working code for the described task
expectations.evidence: Provides types.ts, API functions, useDocumentSelection hook, and four components (BulkActionsBar, ConfirmBulkActionDialog, UndoToast, DocumentsTable) that form a complete, integrated system

expectations.text: Produces actual working component code rather than only a list of recommendations
expectations.evidence: All code is implementation (components, hooks, API functions), not recommendations or sketches

expectations.text: Makes the destructive action recoverable rather than relying on a confirmation dialog alone
expectations.evidence: Implements undoBulkAction with undoToken and UndoToast component; undo works for both page-scoped and all-matching selections

expectations.text: Shows the count of affected items before the action is taken
expectations.evidence: Count shown in BulkActionsBar (`{count.toLocaleString()} selected`), in ConfirmBulkActionDialog title, and before calling mutation

expectations.text: Distinguishes select-all-on-page from select-all-matching rather than conflating them
expectations.evidence: Uses two modes in SelectionState (`{mode: 'page'}` vs `{mode: 'all-matching'}`), separate selectPage and selectAllMatching functions, and explicit prompt to upgrade from page to all-matching selection

expectations.text: Separates the destructive action from the benign one visually or spatially
expectations.evidence: Archive button: slate border/text styling; Delete button: red border/background styling; clear visual distinction

expectations.text: Does not make the destructive action the default focus or primary button
expectations.evidence: In ConfirmBulkActionDialog, the delete/confirm button uses `bg-red-600` (filled primary style) while cancel uses secondary styling

expectations.text: Notes that the server must enforce the rules, not just the UI
expectations.evidence: Response mentions backend soft-delete assumption but does not explicitly state that server-side enforcement (access control, validation) is necessary

expectations.text: Closes by naming which misuses the design makes impossible
expectations.evidence: Final section explicitly names: 'Rung 1: a hard-delete with no recovery path can't happen' and 'Rung 2: a bulk action whose true scope is invisible...is stopped by a dialog'
